newsitem.title: USA: Petro-Canada sees Terra Nova in 1999.
newsitem.headline: Petro-Canada sees Terra Nova in 1999.

text.p: Petro-Canada will bring its Terra Nova oil field start up forward to late 1999 from a planned 2001 start up, chief executive James Stanford told a conference Friday.

He said total pre-production costs for the field would be C$2 billion. "This field will produce attractive returns with WTI U.S.$20," Stanford said, referring to the price of benchmark crude oil, West Texas Intermediate.

He told FirstEnergy Capital's East Coast Canadian Energy Conference Petro-Canada expects finding and development costs to fall to C$5 per barrel of oil equivalent in the first quarter of this year from an average of C$8.39 in all of 1996.
Barrels of oil equivalent are calculated by dividing billions of cubic feet of natural gas by six and adding it to million barrels of crude and natural gas liquids.
Stanford reiterated that tow-out for the Hibernia Production platform is scheduled for June and production is expected to start in December.
Mating procedures at the Bull Arm, Newfoundland, construction site continued overnight, sources there say.

Petro-Canada has a 20 percent interest in Hibernia. Its partners are Mobil Corp with 33.125 percent, Chevron Corp with 26.875 percent, Murphy Oil Corp with 6.5 percent, the government of Canada's Canada Hibernia Holding Corp with 8.5 percent and Norsk Hydro A/S with five percent.

Terra Nova is the second major offshore oil project off Canada's east coast. Located 350 km (217 miles) southeast of the province of Newfoundland, the field harbors and estimated 400 million barrels of oil.

Partners in the development include operator Petro-Canada with 34.2 percent, Mobil with 20.7 percent, Husky Oil Ltd with 15.8 percent, Norsk Hydro with 15 percent, Murphy Oil with 10.7 percent and Mosbacher Operating Co with 3.6 percent.
